messages:
maria: Quick sync idea — propose adding a small "status_verbosity" contract to client responses so we can vary how much internal routing/telemetry detail we expose per customer tier. goal: no accidental internal leak for public tier, but give enterprise customers an actionable hint (eg: which region, fallback tier, quota bucket) :thinking:

aj: curious — is this purely cosmetic (console/SDK) or do clients rely on these fields for retry logic?

maria: primarily cosmetic + hinting. we will NOT change retry semantics. retry decisions should remain based on stable HTTP codes + idempotency guidance. status_verbosity would only control extra fields like `routing_hint`, `capacity_tier`, `internal_code` (redacted for public).

kevin: i worry about SDK churn. if we add fields, older SDKs might surface raw strings. can we keep namespaced keys like `x_redwood:{brief|full}`? that way SDKs can opt-in to parse.

maria: yep — thinking along those lines. proposal: response includes `status_hint_level` = "minimal" | "standard" | "full". then a `status_hint` object with different shapes depending on level. default for hosted free accounts = minimal.

sylvia: console UX question — when a customer's request shows a minimal hint, operators will still want to see full details in their dashboard. do we plan to send full details to the console (backend) always and only redact on the user-facing API response?

maria: yes — telemetry and internal logs always get full detail. only the outward API contract gets tier-based redact. console reads from internal logs so enterprise UI is unaffected.

nate-oncall: for incidents, we need a consistent `telemetry_error_code` that maps 1:1 to internal error taxonomy. even if we redact human-readable hints, telemetry should keep stable error ids so oncall playbooks work. can we add `telemetry_code: string` field (always present) and keep it opaque but stable?

kevin: agree. SDKs should treat `telemetry_code` as opaque. only our internal tooling will map it to playbooks.

aj: edge case: quota vs capacity. customers need to know when to back off vs try again. do we propose separate codes for `quota_exceeded` vs `serve_capacity_shortage`? mixing them in a single "unavailable" will cause bad retry UX.

maria: yes — do distinct canonical client errors. mapping: 429 -> quota_exceeded (with `quota_reset_ms` when available); 503 -> capacity_unavailable (with `suggested_backoff_ms`); 502/504 -> transient_gateway. keep HTTP semantics intact but attach stable client_error codes.

sylvia: for console rollouts we also need to show when we intentionally degrade status_verbosity during canaries. rollout-bot should post a note when we toggle a tier mapping so support sees a timeline.

rollout-bot: automated: rollout 2026-05-01T15:20Z — toggled status_verbosity mapping for org-tier=free -> minimal.

nate-oncall: telemetry tagging: add `err_taxonomy_v` header to internal logs so we can evolve codes without ambiguity. versioning prevents us from reusing numeric ids.

kevin: backward compatibility — please ensure the field names are prefixed to avoid collisions: `x_rw_status_hint_level`, `x_rw_status_hint`, `x_rw_telemetry_code`. SDKs can surface them under nicer names later.

maria: draft response shape (server -> client):

```json
{
  "http_status": 503,
  "client_error": "capacity_unavailable",
  "message": "Service temporarily unavailable",
  "x_rw_status_hint_level": "minimal",
  "x_rw_status_hint": { /* minimal: only public_safe string */ "hint": "try again later" },
  "x_rw_telemetry_code": "C_2032",
  "request_id": "req_abc123"
}
```

maria: and when `status_hint_level` = "full":

```json
{
  "http_status": 503,
  "client_error": "capacity_unavailable",
  "message": "Service temporarily unavailable — high load in us-west-2",
  "x_rw_status_hint_level": "full",
  "x_rw_status_hint": { "region": "us-west-2", "capacity_pool": "dedicated-1", "suggested_backoff_ms": 1200 },
  "x_rw_telemetry_code": "C_2032",
  "request_id": "req_abc123"
}
```

aj: looks good. will the console surface `suggested_backoff_ms` to users or only to ops? might be abused by naive clients.

sylvia: console will show it on the API logs detail pane for their org but not in quickstart docs. we should add a doc blurb: "do not rely on suggested_backoff_ms for precise retry timing — it's a hint".

nate-oncall: for SLOs, we need to ensure that any additional data emitted doesn't count toward high-cardinality tags in metrics systems. prefer sending `capacity_pool` as hashed id in telemetry to avoid cardinality explosion.

kevin: action items: 1) api-schema PR with new fields (maria) 2) sdk guidance doc (kevin) 3) console: show hint mapping + rollout notices (sylvia) 4) telemetry: err_taxonomy_v + hashed fields (nate-oncall) 5) rollout-bot integration to announce toggles (eng-infra)

maria: i'll open the PR today with RFC notes and sample payloads. will cc @kevin @sylvia @nate-oncall. thanks :+1:

aj: sounds good to me. :shipit:

kevin: +1. small ask — include a migration note: "how old SDKs will see unknown fields" (they should ignore unknowns).

sylvia: i'll schedule a quick console design sync after the PR lands.

maria: summary: keep HTTP semantics, add stable `client_error` values and opaque `x_rw_telemetry_code`, implement tiered `x_rw_status_hint_level` redact policy, console reads full internal logs, telemetry always contains full idempotent codes and hashed high-card fields. PR inbound.
